messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Node ephemeral-storage pressure detected on node-az3-gpu-07. 87% ephemeral-storage used, kubelet eviction in 3m. Affected pods: runtime/modelcache-*, runtime/ingest-worker-3 (OOMKills observed). PagerDuty: paging oncall-ingest :rotating_light:

sarah: paging oncall-ingest — seeing multiple runtime crashes + pod evictions in prod. Customer-facing latency spikes reported. Can you take first touch?

oncall-ingest: I'm on it. Looking at node metrics now. Which customers show errors? Any active canaries?

mike: CX alert for customer "ScaleMaps" and several internal canaries. Logs show repeated modelcache writes and a profiler sidecar dumping large files to /tmp/model-dumps every 2m. Disk usage growth matches those timestamps.

devon: confirmed node /var/lib/kubelet/pods/.../volumes/kubernetes.io~empty-dir/model-cache is 95% full on az3-gpu-07. Kubelet eviction threshold approaching. Also seeing container logs: 
```
E2026-03-15T15:19:11Z runtime: ModelCachePersist failed: write /tmp/model-dumps/dump-20260315-...: ENOSPC
E2026-03-15T15:19:11Z runtime: fatal: runtime crash: out of disk space while writing cache
```

katie: Ops-bot shows repeated debug-level traces from runtime-profiling service that were supposed to be disabled in prod. Looks like a config flip pushed debug=true to that sidecar earlier today.

oncall-ingest: Plan: cordon node-az3-gpu-07, drain non-critical pods, delete large profiling dumps, restart modelcache pods with reduced cache size, and roll traffic to az3-gpu-02/04. Also trigger canary fallback to smaller model variant for ScaleMaps. Any objections?

alice: +1. Recommend we also patch the daemonset to set emptyDir medium=sizeLimit and limit the size or set ephemeral-storage requests to avoid host fill. ASAP delete the oldest dumps to free space.

mike: commands I'm running now: 
```
kubectl cordon node-az3-gpu-07
kubectl drain node-az3-gpu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force --grace-period=30
ssh ops@az3-gpu-07 'sudo du -sh /var/lib/kubelet/pods/*/volumes/*/model-cache | sort -h | tail -n 20'
kubectl exec -n runtime runtime-profiling-xxxxx -- rm -rf /tmp/model-dumps/*
kubectl rollout restart deployment/modelcache -n runtime
```

oncall-ingest: Doing the cordon/drain now. Dropping a note to customers: "We're investigating increased errors and latency; we've taken mitigating actions and will update within 15 minutes."

incident-bot: PagerDuty: oncall-ingest accepted the page (incident priority: P1). Incident channel created.

devon: After deleting ~60GB of profiling dumps, node ephemeral usage dropped to 54%. Kubelet evictions stopped. However, we saw two runtime pods crash with CUDA allocation errors in the logs right after restart: 
```
E2026-03-15T15:28:05Z cuda: failed to allocate 312MB: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
E2026-03-15T15:28:06Z runtime: panic: attempt to access freed nv_buffer
```

katie: That smell suggests the restarts triggered GPU allocation races — likely because pods came back with full cache sizes. We need to restart with smaller --max-cache-mb and let them warm up slowly. I'll patch the deployment to set env MODEL_CACHE_MB=512 for the next rollout.

oncall-ingest: Patch applied and scaled down modelcache replicas to 2 to reduce simultaneous GPU warmups. Also set liveness probe backoff to 30s to avoid restart storms.

mike: Rolling restart done. Observed one more CUDA OOM during first warmup on az3-gpu-02; autoscaler drained that pod and rescheduled. No further OOMs after we reduced cache size and limited parallel restarts.

sarah: Customer impact summary so far: ScaleMaps experienced 5 error 500s during the window 15:18–15:30. Internal canaries showed latency spike ~2–3x. No data loss. Mitigation: profiling disabled, deleted dumps, cordon/drain, reduced cache size and replica concurrency, applied fallback to smaller model for ScaleMaps.

ops-bot: ACTIONS TAKEN: [cordoned node-az3-gpu-07] [deleted /tmp/model-dumps ~60GB] [patched deployment/modelcache MODEL_CACHE_MB=512] [scaled replicas -> 2] [rolled back profiler config debug=false].

alice: Follow-ups: 1) Add a deploy-time check to prevent debug=true in prod config. 2) Add limit/size to emptyDir used by modelcache and profiler sidecars. 3) Add alert for sudden ephemeral growth >20GB in 5m. 4) Postmortem runbook updates for GPU warmup concurrency.

oncall-ingest: I'm creating a short incident ticket and assigning follow-ups to infra (emptyDir limits) and runtime (safe cache warmup). Will notify ScaleMaps and share timeline.

sarah: Thanks team. Marking incident as mitigated at 1834503987. We'll keep the channel open for postmortem drafting. :thumbsup:
